definitions.explanation: Used in formal writing to refer back to something mentioned.

examples.japanese: ⟦{同僚|どうりょう}→同僚：01023_douryou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{昼食|ちゅうしょく}→昼食：01616_chuushoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I had lunch with a colleague.

examples.japanese: ⟦{同時|どうじ}→同時：01592_douji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{二|ふた}つ→二つ：02953_futatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦できない→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: I can't do two things at the same time.

examples.japanese: {同社|どうしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦{新製品|しんせいひん}→新製品：18629_shinseihin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発売|はつばい}→発売：04315_hatsubai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The said company will release a new product next year.
examples.notes: {同|どう} + {社|しゃ} = the same/said company

examples.japanese: ⟦{同年代|どうねんだい}→同年代：22399_dounendai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: I have many friends of the same generation.

examples.japanese: {同氏|どうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦{来日|らいにち}→来日：13060_rainichi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧だ。
examples.english: The said person is scheduled to arrive in Japan tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {同市|どうし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{条例|じょうれい}→条例：08255_jourei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{施行|しこう}→施行：06581_shikou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A new ordinance was enacted in the said city.

notes:
{同|どう}〜 is a prefix meaning 'same' or 'the said.'

COMMON COMPOUNDS (SAME):
- ⟦{同時|どうじ}→同時：01592_douji⟧ (same time; simultaneous)
- ⟦{同僚|どうりょう}→同僚：01023_douryou⟧ (colleague)
- ⟦{同級生|どうきゅうせい}→同級生：03032_doukyuusei⟧ (classmate)
- ⟦{同窓会|どうそうかい}→同窓会：15875_dousoukai⟧ (class reunion; alumni association)
- ⟦{同意|どうい}→同意：05092_doui⟧ (agreement; consent)
- ⟦{同様|どうよう}→同様：01654_douyou⟧ (same; similar)
- ⟦{同居|どうきょ}→同居：09730_doukyo⟧ (living together)
- ⟦{同情|どうじょう}→同情：11954_doujou⟧ (sympathy)

FORMAL/WRITTEN USE (THE SAID):
- {同社|どうしゃ} (the said company)
- {同氏|どうし} (the said person)
- {同日|どうじつ} (the same day; that day)

This usage appears frequently in news articles and formal writing.
